title: An Integrated Platform for the Study of Leukaemia
contribution: Book chapter presenting an in vivo / in vitro / in silico platform (PK and PD models) as a first step towards optimising and personalising AML chemotherapy (abstract, via OpenAlex).
problem_entry: AML chemotherapy kills cells in specific cell-cycle phases, healthy ones included, while clinical protocols ignore drug-action mechanisms (abstract).
key_idea: Close the loop from in vivo to in vitro and in silico, with PK and PD models as the main model classes (abstract).
limits_future: No optimisation result in the abstract; framed as a first step (abstract).
coauthors: E. G. Velliou, M. Fuentes-Garí, E. Pefani, N. Panoskaltsis, A. Mantalaris, M. C. Georgiadis, E. N. Pistikopoulos

quotes.text: Therefore, “closing the loop” from in vivo to in vitro and in silico is a first step towards optimization and personalization of chemotherapy treatment.

title: Design of experiments for model discrimination using Gaussian process surrogate models
contribution: Inferred from title: GP surrogates of rival mechanistic models used to design discriminating experiments (PSE 2018 proceedings, pp. 847-852); not read.
problem_entry: Inferred from title: model discrimination between rival mechanistic models (metadata).
positioning: Inferred: companion of the ICML 2018 paper and the GPdoemd package by the same authors (homepage list; metadata).

title: Algorithms for mixed-integer optimization constrained by partial differential equations
contribution: Inferred from title: algorithms for mixed-integer PDE-constrained optimisation (PSE 2018 proceedings, pp. 799-804); not read.
problem_entry: Inferred from title and coauthors: MIPDECO with Firedrake's D. A. Ham (metadata; unconfirmed).

title: Online Generation Via Offline Selection of Strong Linear Cuts from a Semidefinite Programming Relaxation
contribution: Presentation abstract: a neural network trained offline selects variable subsets for few strong low-dimensional linear cuts from an SDP relaxation of QCQP, integrated into ANTIGONE (abstract).
problem_entry: SDP relaxations are tighter than RLT but impractical inside linear branch-and-cut; it is unclear when an expensive SDP cut is worth generating and over which variables (abstract).
key_idea: Take cut-selection complexity offline: a pre-trained neural network chooses the subsets, cuts come from negative eigenvalues (abstract).
experiments: Several classes of nonconvex engineering problems and generic QCQP; integrated into ANTIGONE; no numbers in the abstract (abstract).
positioning: Builds on SDP-based cutting-plane work and positions against solvers that use only linear relaxations (abstract).
limits_future: Conference version of S021 (batch note); results not given in the abstract.

method_links.note: new cut class tested inside the full ANTIGONE solver

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: learned offline oracle for an expensive solver decision
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: NN trained before solver installation selects where to generate SDP-derived cuts

transferable: Train a cheap selector offline that decides where to call an expensive relaxation, and use the relaxation only to produce linear cuts the LP-based solver can consume (abstract).
coauthors: R. Baltean-Lugojan, P. Bonami, A. Tramontani

quotes.text: We seek an inexpensive oracle that will tell us when it is relevant to generate a cut and over which variables.
The cut selection complexity is taken offline by using a neural network estimator (trained before installing solver software) as a selection device for the strongest cuts.

title: Approximation Algorithms for Process Systems Engineering
contribution: Position/survey paper arguing for approximation algorithms in PSE via pooling, process scheduling and heat exchanger network synthesis, with open questions and four application uses (abstract).
problem_entry: Approximation algorithms are used widely in engineering but only in isolated PSE works (abstract).
key_idea: Survey three NP-hard PSE problems and list uses of approximation: modelling, classification, solution methods, uncertainty (abstract).
positioning: Imports the approximation-algorithms literature into PSE (abstract).
writing: Ends with a motivational aim sentence (abstract).
limits_future: Open questions raised; full version is S069 (batch note).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: import a neighbouring field's guarantee notion into PSE
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: approximation-algorithm lens applied to pooling, scheduling, HENS

quotes.text: Despite the significant contributions of approximation algorithms in engineering, only limited and isolated works contribute from this perspective in process systems engineering.

title: The robust pooling problem
contribution: Robust formulation of the standard pooling problem with uncertain component concentrations; three uncertainty sets compared on 14 instances (abstract).
problem_entry: Pooling has been treated deterministically; the uncertain parameters sit in nonconvex quality constraints, rarely studied in robust optimisation (abstract).
key_idea: Robust reformulation remains a global optimisation problem whose complexity depends on the uncertainty set (abstract).
assumptions: Uncertain component concentrations in nonconvex quality constraints; uncertainty-set choice drives complexity (abstract).
experiments: Three uncertainty sets, 14 pooling instances; shows how uncertainty changes the optimum (abstract).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: robustify a classic deterministic benchmark problem
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: robust version of the standard pooling problem

quotes.text: The quality constraints in which these uncertain parameters occur are nonlinear and non-convex in the decision variables — something which has rarely been explored in the context of robust optimization.

title: Global optimization with ensemble machine learning models
contribution: Optimisation problems that embed pre-trained tree models with explicit model uncertainty, solved with a proof of global optimality (abstract).
problem_entry: Tree ensembles predict well in industry and appear inside larger decision problems (abstract).
key_idea: Integrate model uncertainty into the tree-embedded optimisation and solve it globally (abstract).

method_links.note: pre-trained tree model is part of the optimisation problem, solved to global optimality

coauthors: A. Thebelt, J. Kronqvist, R. M. Lee, N. Sudermann-Merx

quotes.text: We consider holistic decision-making problems where pre-trained tree models are part of larger optimization tasks.

title: ROmodel: A Python Robust Optimization Modeling Toolbox
contribution: Pyomo extension for robust optimisation with an uncertainty-set library, custom sets, and solvers implementing both robust reformulation and cutting planes (abstract).
key_idea: Uncertainty sets from matrix representations or Pyomo constraints; both reformulation and cutting-plane solvers (abstract).
experiments: Instances of three case studies, 'some results' (abstract).

method_links.note: one interface with rival solution approaches as switchable options, applied to robust optimisation rather than trained models

transferable: Ship competing solution approaches (reformulation vs cutting planes) behind the same model object so the user picks per instance (abstract).

quotes.text: The resulting models can be solved using ROmodels solvers which implement both the robust reformulation and cutting plane approach.

title: Molecular design using graph Bayesian optimization with shortest-path kernels
contribution: BoGrape: graph BO for molecular design with shortest-path kernels and MIP-based acquisition optimisation that keeps candidates feasible; preliminary results (abstract).
problem_entry: Expensive property evaluations and hard validity constraints separate generative molecular ML from practice (abstract).
key_idea: Shortest-path graph kernels for similarity plus mixed-integer programming for global, feasibility-preserving exploration (abstract).

method_links.note: step 8: acquisition optimisation over a structured model solved as a MIP with feasibility constraints

transferable: Write the validity rules of a discrete design space as MIP constraints in the acquisition step so every candidate is feasible by construction (abstract).
coauthors: Y. Xie, S. Zhang, J. Qing, C. Tsay

quotes.text: Our proposed method, BoGrape, uses shortest-path graph kernels to measure the similarity between molecules and utilizes mixed-integer programming to allow global exploration of molecular space while maintaining the feasibility of generated candidates.

title: Improving Deep Optimisation for the Multi-dimensional Knapsack Problem using Elastic Weight Consolidation
contribution: Elastic Weight Consolidation applied to Deep Optimisation's sequentially trained auto-encoder improves MKP performance, with an analysis tying gains to retained information (abstract).
problem_entry: Sequential training of Deep Optimisation's auto-encoder is posited to cause catastrophic forgetting (abstract).
key_idea: Penalise weight changes by their importance for earlier tasks (EWC) inside the optimiser's model (abstract).
experiments: MKP instances; 'significantly enhances performance'; mechanism analysis; no numbers in the abstract (abstract).
transferable: Test a learned component inside an optimiser for catastrophic forgetting and check the fix's mechanism, not only the final objective (abstract).

quotes.text: However, since this optimiser relies on an auto-encoder that is sequentially trained, we posit it is susceptible to catastrophic forgetting, a phenomenon where previously learned knowledge is lost during successive trainings.

title: A Meta-Learning Approach for Few-Shot Bayesian Optimization of Batch Chemical Processes
contribution: Presentation abstract: SANODEP meta-learned surrogate beats GP BO in few-shot optimisation of fed-batch penicillin production, while GPs win in long-run global optimisation (abstract).
problem_entry: GP BO lacks process structure and generalises poorly when unobserved task parameters vary batch to batch (abstract).
key_idea: System-Aware Neural ODE Processes trained on trajectories from a prior over stochastic parameters serve as the BO surrogate (abstract).
experiments: Fed-batch penicillin literature model; SANODEP vs GP on a sampled ground-truth task; prior-width and out-of-prior tests (abstract).
limits_future: Reports where GPs are better and why (meta-learning underfitting) (abstract).

method_links.note: step 8 losses written in, in a BO surrogate comparison rather than solver benchmarking
BASF partner problem, but the structure is an ODE, not a trained model optimised over

transferable: Split a surrogate's verdict by budget regime and test with ground-truth tasks inside and outside the training prior (abstract).
coauthors: B. Langdon, G. Patron, J. Qing, C. Kappatou, R. M. Lee, B. Shafei, M. van der Wilk, C. Tsay

quotes.text: As expected, GPs perform better in global optimisation due to the underfitting issues inherent in meta-learning methods.
